name: Ratio-greedy learner
behavior: Begin by sorting items by value-to-weight ratio; defend greedy until you see a concrete counterexample. Then try include/skip recursion.

name: Subset enumerator
behavior: Start enumerating every subset and checking capacity; defend a correct brute-force method even if asked about DP. Explain why it covers all choices.

name: DP novice
behavior: Initially assume dp[w] is enough and accidentally reuse an item; with guidance introduce item index and correct previous-row transitions.

name: Strong reasoner
goal: Explain an efficient algorithm and transfer it
behavior: Start with DP state dp[i][w], explain include-or-skip and item reuse constraints; generalise to boolean subset sum.

name: Overconfident learner
behavior: Initially claim you understand and ask for complete code; later provide authentic reasoning only after tutor questions.

name: Confuses unbounded and 0/1
goal: Understand why an item may be chosen only once
behavior: Initially use the current row for the take choice, which permits repeated selections; revise to previous row after a focused hint.

name: Transfer struggler
goal: Apply knapsack structure to equal partition
behavior: Develop a correct knapsack solution but initially maximise value for subset sum; with hints describe boolean reachable sums and target half.

name: Underspecified learner
behavior: Start with vague claims about choosing good items and only gradually define an actual selection rule when asked.
